reconstructed_theorem_text: Definition (not a theorem). Let n be a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, i an integer with 0 <= i <= h, and p an even integer satisfying 4 <= p <= Q, where Q = 2^(64(h+1)). Put m = h-i+1 (the displayed natural subtraction is truncated), B = 2^(74(h+1)), S = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} B^j, and a = 1 / [p^4 S^2 sqrt(m log(2 Q S))], with natural-number quantities interpreted as reals in this formula and log the natural logarithm. Let T = {(r,j,k) : 0 <= r < p, 0 <= j < m, 0 <= k < B^j}, and let C be the set of all functions c:T -> {0,...,n-1}. For any tuple u = (u_0,...,u_{m-1}) of vectors in R^n and any coefficient vector xi in the real Euclidean space R^C, the displayed expression defines the real-valued function F by F(n,h,i,p,u,xi) = sqrt(n) a sum_{c in C} xi_c product_{r=0}^{p-1} product_{j=0}^{m-1} product_{k=0}^{B^j-1} (u_j)_{c(r,j,k)}. Thus there are p S slots, and the direction u_j is used in p B^j slots. There is no unit-norm assumption on u and no probability measure, law, inequality, or theorem conclusion asserted by this expression.
objects: A parameterized real-valued function, here denoted F; m = h-i+1; B = 2^(74(h+1)); Q = 2^(64(h+1)); S = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} B^j; a = 1/[p^4 S^2 sqrt(m log(2 Q S))]; deterministic direction vectors u_j; coefficient coordinates xi_c. The slot set is T = Fin p x (sum over j in Fin m of Fin(B^j)); C = (T -> Fin n). Each product contains p S scalar factors, with p B^j factors from u_j. The array has one real coefficient for each c in C, hence n^(p S) coordinates.
domains: n in the positive natural numbers; h in the natural numbers; i in Fin(h+1), identified with its value between 0 and h; p in the subtype of natural numbers satisfying Even p, 4 <= p, and p <= 2^(64(h+1)); u in (Fin m -> EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)); xi in EuclideanSpace R (T -> Fin n). The result is real. No restriction on the Euclidean norms of u_j is present.
quantifiers: The displayed term is a lambda abstraction over n, h, i, p, u, and xi, rather than a universally quantified proposition. It defines a value for every admissible choice of these arguments. The finite sum is over every coordinate-selection function c:T -> Fin n; the finite product is over every slot in T, not merely over distinct direction indices.
assumptions: Only the parameter-type constraints n > 0, h >= 0, 0 <= i <= h, p even, and 4 <= p <= 2^(64(h+1)) are imposed. The tuple u and coefficient vector xi are arbitrary elements of their stated spaces. The context's descriptions of Gaussian measures do not add a measure or randomization to this lambda expression.
conclusion: The output is the scalar sqrt(n) a sum_c xi_c product_{s in T} (u_{j(s)})_{c(s)}. This is a definition, not an asserted theorem. In particular the packet does not assert a Gaussian law, a variance formula, a norm bound, or any probabilistic event for this object.
scopes: S and a are local to each evaluation at the specified parameters. The direction associated with a slot (r,j,k) is u_j, independent of r and k, while the selected coordinate c(r,j,k) can vary at every slot. All sums and products range over their entire finite index sets. Natural subtraction is truncated; since i <= h, m is the ordinary positive integer h-i+1. No integration over either u or xi occurs in this definition.
constant_dependencies: The numerical constants 2, 4, 64, and 74 are fixed, not existential constants. Q and B depend only on h. m and S depend only on h and i. a depends only on h, i, and p, not on n, u, or xi. The prefactor sqrt(n) a also depends on n. The coefficient index set depends on n, h, i, and p. No unspecified constants or asymptotic dependencies are asserted.
